chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man: should he recite aloud in supererogatory prayer during the day? He said: “Yes.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This narration is a concession, and what is more virtuous is that nothing in the daytime prayers should be recited aloud, and nothing from the nighttime prayers should be recited quietly; that is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.الْأَفْضَلُ: what is more virtuous or preferable

ai.seo_question: May one recite aloud in voluntary prayers during the daytime?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of audible recitation in supererogatory prayer during the daytime. The Imam عليه السلام permits it, while Shaykh al-Ṭūsī notes that this report indicates a concession, and that the more virtuous practice is quiet recitation in daytime prayers and audible recitation in nighttime prayers.
